roof_pitch.rule_append: Narrower than the family's own 3:12-9:12 band: 4:12 to 6:12 (soft constraint c05) so that any gable reads as a pediment. Pitches above 8:12 push the building toward Gothic Revival.

dormer.rule_append: Where an upper half-storey is habitable it is lit through frieze-band windows, not a dormer, and a frieze window and a dormer must never appear on the same elevation (hard constraint c03) -- the frieze-band attic window is the style's own quietly ingenious substitute for the dormer the inherited Georgian roof relies on.

storey_diminution_required.note: Deliberately breaks the inherited Federal and Georgian diminishing-storey rule rather than merely adjusting it: this style unifies the whole facade height behind one continuous entablature carried on full-height columns, and its own typical_ratios name no diminution ratio at all, unlike federal-style's explicit 0.80-0.90 / 0.60-0.75.

ceiling_height_ft.source: storey-graduation pack authority note, 'Greek Revival 10-12 ft'

height_proportion.rule: The column height equals the full facade height of the block it fronts, without exception in canonical work (proportional_system); the eye is not asked to read a graduated hierarchy of storeys behind the portico, because the order unifies them into one volume.

variants.note: Promoted from permitted: a broad flat corner pilaster board is the style's standard corner treatment, not a decorative option among several.

corner_pilaster_width_in.note: Overrides the inherited Federal 1-1/4 in board-THICKNESS ceiling, which is a different dimension (thickness, not width) and remains compatible: the Greek Revival corner is a wide, flat, thin board, not a thick or deeply projecting one.

cornice_of_entablature_ratio.source: greek-revival-american proportional_system: architrave : frieze : cornice approximately 3 : 3 : 2
cornice_of_entablature_ratio.note: The cornice is the '2' of the 3:3:2 subdivision, i.e. one quarter of the full entablature depth.

cornice.rule: The cornice is the corona of a full entablature run continuously as a deep horizontal band around the building -- not the shallow, Federal-thinned corona that overrides this slot on the style's own parent -- and it is not reduced below constraint c02's floor: a cornice thinner than 1/8 of column height reads as Federal or Colonial Revival regardless of the columns below it.

frieze_window_height_max_ratio.source: greek-revival-american constraint c03: frieze-band windows 'no taller than one third of the frieze depth'

frieze.rule: A deep frieze band, 10 to 20 in, carried continuously under the eave, frequently pierced by small horizontal windows lighting a habitable attic (constraint c03) -- this is the diagnostic tell the style names before any other: small horizontal windows set into the frieze board directly under the eave, which no other American style does.

special_window.rule: No special window: no Palladian, no Venetian, no lunette, no oculus. Greek vocabulary is exclusive (constraint c04) and every one of the family's special windows depends on a curve or an arch this style eliminates; the habitable attic is lit through the frieze band instead (see frieze), not through a special window form.

variants.note: Broad flat pilasters carrying a heavy flat entablature -- Greek Revival's rectangular answer to the Georgian pedimented frontispiece and the Federal fanlight alike.
On the grandest examples, matching the order of the main portico.
Blocked and rusticated jambs are a Georgian device this style forbids alongside every other arch-derived or curved ornament (constraint c04).
The Federal signature this style's own distinguished_from clause names directly against it: 'elliptical rather than rectangular transom lights'.
Curved, Baroque-derived ornament; excluded by the same vocabulary discipline as arches and domes (constraint c04).
Same objection as broken-scroll-pediment.
The entrance is where the style concentrates its whole classical vocabulary; a bare opening is not this style at any scale, from the plainest upland farmhouse to the largest plantation portico.

door_surround.rule: A rectangular opening framed by broad flat pilasters carrying a heavy flat entablature at least 12 in deep, inside a pilastered surround -- no curve, no ellipse, no rustication anywhere in the assembly.

variants.note: The single fastest Federal/Greek Revival discriminator on a plain house: rectangular, never curved.
Optional rather than required -- unlike Federal, where the fanlight requires them.
The Federal signature this style eliminates outright (defining_characteristics: 'elliptical fanlights eliminated').
Same exclusion as elliptical-fanlight; a round-headed transom is a Roman/Jeffersonian or Georgian device, not this style's.

transom_sidelight.rule: The entrance is a rectangular opening with a rectangular transom, sidelights optional, inside the pilastered surround (constraint c04) -- door transom shape is the single fastest Federal/Greek Revival discriminator on a plain house.

variants.note: Baseless, 5.5-7 lower diameters. The order's own defining_characteristics: 'baseless fluted Doric, Greek Ionic, or the Tower-of-the-Winds Corinthian; no Roman arches, no domes, no Composite'.
8.5-9.5 diameters. No Benjamin/dedicated Greek Ionic pack exists in this corpus; the style's own binding of plain vignola-ionic is an honest stand-in, its 9-diameter column landing inside this range.
The Tower-of-the-Winds type specifically, about 10 diameters -- named in the style's own typical_ratios, rare relative to Doric and Ionic.
A base under a Doric order means Roman, which means Jeffersonian or a later revival, per this style's own diagnostic_tells.
The Adam-attenuated Federal order this style thickens against, per its own reacts_against lineage edge.
Roman, and absent from the style's own three named Greek orders.
Explicitly excluded in defining_characteristics: 'no Composite'.
The upland vernacular's trim-only expression carries the proportion without a built order at all; see greek-revival-upland-vernacular.

authority.value: Asher Benjamin, The Architect, or Practical House Carpenter (1830); Minard Lafever, The Beauties of Modern Architecture (1835); James Stuart and Nicholas Revett, The Antiquities of Athens (1762-1830), at fourth hand through the handbooks

order.rule: Greek orders only -- baseless fluted Doric, Greek Ionic, or the rare Tower-of-the-Winds Corinthian -- taken at second or third hand from Stuart and Revett through Benjamin and Lafever; no Roman arches, domes, Composite, or base under a Doric column.

variants.note: Roman, not Greek, and a base under a Doric order rules the building out of this style regardless of the rest of its trim.
Adam-attenuated Federal proportion.
The upland vernacular's carpenter answer where a built order is not affordable at all.

height_diameters_doric.source: benjamin-doric pack (7 diameters); Parthenon Doric is 5.5

base.value: none under Doric; a base is permitted under Ionic and Corinthian only

construction.value: built up of staves like a barrel and hollow inside, flutes gouged not applied, shaft entasis carried through the joint, ventilated at cap and base
construction.source: greek-revival-northern constraint c05, generalised to the style

column.rule: The column is thickened rather than thinned -- 5.5 to 7 diameters for Doric, 8.5 to 9.5 for Ionic -- sitting directly on the porch deck with no base under a Doric order; in wood it is built up of staves rather than turned solid, and the illusion of stone is completed in white lead paint.

total_height_ratio.source: greek-revival-american constraint c02: 'entablature depth must be 1/4 to 1/5 of column height'

min_ratio_reads_as_federal.note: Below 1/8 of column height the entablature reads as Federal or Colonial Revival regardless of the columns below it.

entablature.rule: The single most diagnostic ratio in the style: entablature depth is 1/4 to 1/5 of column height, subdivided architrave : frieze : cornice at approximately 3 : 3 : 2 -- the exact proportional inversion of the Federal entablature this style reacts against.

variants.note: Curved, Baroque-derived furniture logic; excluded outright by this style's vocabulary discipline (constraint c04), not merely restricted to doorways.
Same exclusion as broken-scroll.
A segmental (curved) pediment is an arch-derived form; constraint c04 forbids round-headed arches in every other guise and this is the same exclusion applied to the pediment.

rise_over_span.source: greek-revival-american proportional_system: 'pediment height 1/4.5 to 1/5.5 of its span'

pediment.rule_append: Where no full pediment is built, the cornice must return at least 12 in onto the gable end (constraint c05) -- the cheapest possible gesture toward a pediment, and the commonest single Greek Revival tell in vernacular work.

pilaster.rule: A broad, flat, unmoulded pilaster board, 8 to 14 in wide -- ornament by profile and mass rather than by relief carving, and against the Federal pilaster's 3 in projection cap this is width, not depth, doing the work.

variants.note: The Doric entablature's own cornice runs on guttae and mutules, not a modillion or dentil course; where Doric governs, the bed mould is plain.
Correct under an Ionic or Corinthian order, not under Doric.
The Federal-thinned and Georgian modillion block; this style's cornice depth is carried by mass and projection, not by a run of carved blocks.
The Doric signature -- 'correctly detailed with triglyphs, metopes and guttae' per this style's own exemplar note on Berry Hill.
Only where the rare Tower-of-the-Winds Corinthian order is used; not a general-purpose motif here.
The upland vernacular strain runs no carved ornament at all; the trim widths alone carry the classical reading.
Adamesque and Federal. Excluded here on the same reacts_against logic that makes this style's own entablature the proportional inverse of Federal's.
Federal low-relief applied ornament; this style carves in mass, not in applied composition.
Federal, pendant and thin; the opposite register from this style's broad flat trim.
The Adam oval, a Federal signature this style is defined against.
Low-relief Adamesque surface treatment; not part of this style's flat-board, mass-and-profile vocabulary.
See modillion_dentil: correct only under Ionic or Corinthian, not the canonical Doric.
See modillion_dentil.

relief.value: carved in mass or built up in wood, never applied composition casting

ornament_vocabulary.rule: Greek vocabulary is exclusive (constraint c04): guttae and triglyphs under the Doric entablature, acanthus reserved for the rare Corinthian order, and no round-headed arch, dome, elliptical fanlight, or Adamesque applied motif anywhere on the building.

variants.note: Full-height, the governing facade gesture: column height equals the full height of the block it fronts, without exception in canonical work.
The temple-front-with-wings and gable-front massings both run a full-width, full-height portico or colonnade across the principal block.
The cheapest vernacular examples reduce to trim boards and a doorway with no portico at all; see greek-revival-upland-vernacular.
A superimposed two-order portico is a Georgian and Southern-colonial device; this style's single continuous entablature runs the full height on one order.
Cutting a loggia into the front breaks the wall plane the full-height portico depends on.
Queen Anne; a Northern Greek Revival house never wraps its colonnade (see greek-revival-southern-plantation for the variant that does, on different grounds).
A Creole and Gulf Coast device, not this style's own vocabulary.
1900-1930, decades after the style's own floruit ends in 1860.

porch_type.rule: A portico whose column height equals the full facade height of the block it fronts (hard constraint c01) -- a two-storey block with one-storey columns is not Greek Revival, it is Colonial Revival or a later hybrid.

variants.note: Sits directly on the porch deck with no base; a base under a Doric column means Roman, which means Jeffersonian or a later revival (this style's own diagnostic_tells).
Roman, based; excluded by the same rule as above.
Roman, not among the style's three named Greek orders.
Greek Ionic at 8.5-9.5 diameters remains one of the style's own three named orders, but Doric is the far commoner porch support.
Inherited rule still holds: a free column with no answering pilaster on the wall behind it reads as furniture stood in front of the house.
The inherited Georgian record already names this id as 'the successor's successor' and forbids it; this style is that successor, and the flip from forbidden to canonical is the point.
Heavier and more deeply modelled than this style's own corner-blocked, pedestal-less trim; mixing families is the interior equivalent of mixing typefaces.
Federal's flattened, applied-composition family is the proportional opposite of this style's heavy carved corner-block trim.

trim_family.rule_append: The pedestal has been abandoned entirely -- heavy symmetrical architraves with corner blocks, deep plain baseboards, a black marble mantel of two square posts and a slab.

height_in.note: 10 1/4 in in only two members, against Georgian's 6 7/8 in in three -- 'the pedestal has been abandoned entirely'.

corner_block.note: Heavy symmetrical architraves with corner blocks are the style's own stated interior signature, distinct from the mitred Georgian and Federal casing this slot otherwise inherits.
